question: The weight of an object on the moon in comparison to earth will be
solution:
The correct answer is__** 6 times less.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The weight of an object on the Moon is approximately **1/6th** of its weight on Earth due to the Moon's lower gravitational pull.
 
• Gravity on the Moon is about **1.62 m/s²**, compared to Earth's gravitational acceleration of approximately **9.81 m/s²**.
 
• This significant difference means that an object will weigh **6 times less** on the Moon than it does on Earth.
 
• Understanding weight differences due to gravitational variation is essential for **space exploration** and **physics**.
 
• The reduced weight on the Moon allows astronauts to move more freely and perform tasks with less effort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight vs. Mass**: Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object, while mass is the amount of matter in the object and remains constant regardless of location.
 
• **Gravitational Force**: The strength of gravity varies on different celestial bodies, affecting how much an object weighs. The Moon's lower gravity is a result of its smaller size and mass compared to Earth.
 
• **Practical Example**: If an object weighs 60 kg on Earth, it would weigh approximately **10 kg** on the Moon.
